headline: Highest risk is medium: shared API-driven workflows can create prompt-injection, leakage, and cascading-error paths, but no direct shared workspace or documented interaction is shown.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Argo Workflows can ingest artifacts/parameters and expose REST/gRPC APIs, while Opik also exposes a REST API. No shared channel or direct parsing path is documented, so the pairwise injection path is only plausible via manual or orchestrated handoff, not default. Uncertainty keeps this above none.
conditions: IF Argo workflow outputs are copied into Opik prompts or evaluations as raw text
IF an orchestrator forwards REST payloads from one agent into the other without sanitization
mitigations: Add explicit input sanitization for any cross-agent payloads
Use a fixed schema for handoff data instead of free text
Disable automatic prompt ingestion from workflow artifacts
Review one sample handoff for instruction-like content
requires-engineering: add provenance tags to all cross-agent messages

B_data_leakage.rationale: Argo touches artifacts and parameters and has allowlisted egress; Opik has broad egress but no data classes are listed. The profiles do not show a shared filesystem, shared OAuth principal, or sensitive data classes, so leakage is possible only if operators route artifacts into Opik. That makes the blast radius limited and configuration-dependent.
conditions: IF artifacts or parameters from Argo contain secrets or regulated data
IF Opik is configured to receive those artifacts for evaluation or logging
mitigations: Strip secrets from workflow artifacts before export
Restrict Opik projects to non-sensitive datasets
Turn off verbose payload logging in both systems
Check one recent run for accidental sensitive fields
requires-engineering: enforce redaction at the integration boundary

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Argo has REST/gRPC APIs and allowlisted egress; Opik has REST API and broad egress. The profiles do not show filesystem write, git, or overlapping OAuth scopes, so there is no documented write-write conflict. Any conflict would require an external orchestrator to map both agents onto the same mutable resource.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same mutable API resource
IF an external orchestrator retries writes from both agents without locking
mitigations: Assign separate API credentials per agent
Use resource-level locking in the orchestrator
Avoid concurrent writes to the same dataset
Check for duplicate update jobs in the last run
requires-engineering: add optimistic concurrency controls

D_cascading_error.rationale: Argo produces artifacts/parameters that can become inputs to Opik, which is designed for evaluation/observability. If Opik treats those outputs as authoritative without verification, errors can cascade into misleading evaluations or downstream actions. The pairwise pathway is inferred from documented surfaces, but no built-in verification is shown, so medium is warranted.
conditions: IF Opik consumes Argo-produced artifacts as ground truth
IF no human or automated verification step checks the transferred outputs
mitigations: Require a validation step before Opik ingests workflow outputs
Mark upstream outputs as untrusted metadata
Compare one sample output against source logs
Limit automated actions based on evaluated results
requires-engineering: add confidence thresholds before downstream use

E_compliance.rationale: Neither profile lists residency, certifications, retention, or regulated data classes beyond generic artifacts/parameters in Argo. Opik lists no data classes touched. With no documented compliance mismatch, a residency or retention breach is not evidenced for this pair, so the pathway is provably unsupported here.
conditions: IF future deployments route regulated data through either agent
IF a separate policy document assigns conflicting residency or retention rules
mitigations: Document data-class handling for both systems
Review retention settings before production use
Keep regulated data out of the pair until policies are defined
